test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II ( JSO ) 2021 Official Paper ( Held On: 10 August 2022 )
subject: general
question:
Fundamental principles of design of experiment are

(I) Randomization

(II) Replication

(III) Local control

Which option is correct?
solution:
The correct answer is **Randomization, Replication and local control.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Randomization is the stage where statistical methods are used to detail the accuracy of the experiment.
 
• Replication is when the basic experiments are repeated to minimise errors.
 
• Local control is used it has been noted that randomization and replication do not entirely eliminate all extraneous sources of variation, leaving them uncontrollable. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​The process of randomly distributing treatments to experimental units is known as randomization. Every conceivable treatment allocation has the same chance under the random process, it is implied.
 
• As a result, the local control technique improves the experiment. In other words, one needs to pick a design that will allow us to control any unneeded sources of variation. One employs local control, which refers to the degree of balancing, blocking, and grouping of experimental units, for this aim. 

**Hence, randomization Replication and Local control are the primary and most essential steps for designing a successful experiment. **
